extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent practitioners, and members of the public seeking the original U.S. patent statute (historical)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the legal requirements and standards set by the United States Patent Act of 1790 for applying for, issuing, recording, challenging, and enforcing patents (petition content, specification/models, novelty/usefulness, procedures, evidence, remedies, and fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to executive officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the petition of any person or persons to the Secretary of State, the Secretary for the department of war, and the Attorney General of the United States, setting forth that he, she, or they hath or have invented or discovered any useful art, manufacture, engine, machine, or device, or any improvement therein not before known or used, and praying that a patent may be granted therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must state the invention/discovery and that it is ‘not before known or used’ and request a patent; it must be presented to the three named officers (Secretary of State, Sec. of War, Attorney General).

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty and usefulness requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Invention or discovery must be 'not before known or used' and be a 'useful art, manufacture, engine, machine, or device, or any improvement therein not before known or used.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute requires novelty (not previously known or used) and usefulness/importance; officers evaluate whether the invention is sufficiently useful and important before issuing a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and form of letters patent; grant scope and term
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of State, the Secretary for the department of war, and the Attorney General, or any two of them, if they shall deem the invention useful and important, may cause letters patent to be issued. Letters patent are to be made out in the name of the United States, to bear teste by the President, reciting the allegations of the petition and describing the invention 'clearly, truly and fully,' granting the sole and exclusive right for any term not exceeding fourteen years 'the sole and exclusive right and liberty of making, constructing, using and vending to others to be used' the said invention or discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents must recite petition allegations and include a clear, true, and full description; the maximum statutory patent term is 14 years; the exclusive rights granted are expressly defined (make, construct, use, vend).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification in writing and accompanying drafts/models (particularity and enablement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees must, at time of granting, deliver to the Secretary of State a specification in writing, containing a description, accompanied with drafts or models, and explanations and models (if the nature of the invention will admit of a model). The specification 'shall be so particular, and said models so exact, as not only to distinguish the invention or discovery from other things before known and used, but also to enable a workman or other person skilled in the art ... to make, construct, or use the same.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes requirements equivalent to distinctness and enablement: the specification and models must both (1) distinguish the invention from prior known things and (2) teach a person skilled in the art how to make/use it so the public benefits after patent expiry. Specifications are to be filed in the Secretary's office and certified copies are competent evidence in courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing, recording, and delivery of patents and specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters patent shall be recorded in a book to be kept for that purpose in the office of the Secretary of State, and delivered to the patentee or his agent, and the delivery shall be entered on the record and endorsed on the patent by the said Secretary at the time of granting the same. Specifications shall be filed in the office of the said Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory recordation and entry of delivery/endorsement by the Secretary of State; filed specifications form part of the public record and evidentiary record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney General examination and certification; presidential seal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Attorney General shall examine the letters patent delivered to him, and within fifteen days, if he finds the same conformable to this Act, certify it to be so at the foot thereof, and present the letters patent so certified to the President, who shall cause the seal of the United States to be thereto affixed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A procedural check: the Attorney General must certify conformity within 15 days before the President affixes the seal—formal steps required for a valid patent under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to specifications and models; permissive copying
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon application to the Secretary of State for a copy of any such specification, and for permission to have similar model or models made, the Secretary must give such copy and permit the person to take or make or cause the same to be made, at the expense of such applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statutory scheme contemplates public inspection and copying of specifications and models (at applicant's expense), promoting dissemination of the invention's details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for unauthorized use (infringement)
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person devises, makes, constructs, uses, employs, or vends within the United States any art, manufacture, engine, machine or device the sole and exclusive right of which shall be granted by patent, without the consent of the patentee, every person so offending shall forfeit and pay to the patentee such damages as shall be assessed by a jury, and moreover shall forfeit to the person aggrieved the thing or things so devised, made, constructed, used, employed or vended, which may be recovered in an action on the case founded on this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory civil remedies include jury-assessed damages and forfeiture/recovery of infringing items via an action on the case; enforcement is through courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to repeal patents obtained surreptitiously or by false suggestion
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon oath or affirmation before the judge of the district court that any patent was obtained surreptitiously by or upon false suggestion, and motion made within one year after issuing the patent (but not afterwards), the judge may grant a rule to show cause and, if sufficient cause is not shown, order process and, if the patentee was not the first and true inventor, judgment shall be rendered for the repeal of such patent or patents; if the complainant loses, he shall pay the costs the defendant was put to defending the suit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A one-year statutory window to challenge a patent on grounds of surreptitious procurement or false suggestion; courts may repeal patents and shift costs to unsuccessful challengers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents and specifications as prima facie evidence; defenses and notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In actions by a patentee for penalties, the patents or specifications shall be prima facie evidence that the patentee was the first and true inventor and that the same is truly specified; nevertheless the defendant may plead the general issue and give this Act, and any special matter (of which notice in writing shall have been given to the plaintiff or his attorney thirty days before the trial), in evidence tending to prove that the specification does not contain the whole truth concerning his invention or that it contains more than is necessary to produce the effect described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents carry evidentiary weight as prima facie proof of priority and sufficiency, but defendants may file particularized defenses (with 30 days' written notice) alleging insufficiency, concealment, or overclaiming; if concealment or inclusion of unnecessary matter is intended to mislead or actually misleads so the claimed effect cannot be produced by specified means, verdict may favor the defendant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and costs for patent issuance and related services
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees to be paid before receipt of patent: for receiving and filing the petition, fifty cents; for filing specifications, per copy-sheet containing one hundred words, ten cents; for making out patent, two dollars; for affixing great seal, one dollar; for indorsing the day of delivering the same to the patentee, including all intermediate services, twenty cents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific statutory fee schedule for petition, specification filing (per 100 words), patent preparation, seal affixation, and endorsement; payment is a precondition to issuance.
